Lapataia Bay lies in the Argentine part of Tierra del Fuego, within Tierra del Fuego National Park. Forests reach the shore, beyond which lie calm water and mountain slopes.

Wooden boardwalks offer a closer look at the coastal landscape. Argentina's National Route No. 3 ends here. Lapataia is visited on excursions from Ushuaia, together with Lake Roca and other parts of the park.

The Larco Museum in Lima introduces visitors to Peruvian cultures that existed long before the Incas. Archaeologist Rafael Larco Hoyle founded the museum in 1926. The collection is housed in an 18th-century colonial mansion built on the site of an earlier pre-Columbian structure.

The museum holds around 45,000 objects. Ceramics, textiles, gold and silver artifacts, ritual objects and archaeological finds reveal how the ancient peoples of Peru lived. A separate section is devoted to Moche ceramics, including pieces depicting erotic scenes.

As part of the tour, a visit to the museum is offered separately on the day of departure from Lima. It can be coordinated with the timing of the airport transfer.
